title: Rwanda Gorilla Permit: Prices, Discounts and How to Book
meta_title: Rwanda Gorilla Permit: Prices, 30% Discount & How to Book
meta_description: Rwanda gorilla permit prices for foreigners, residents and citizens, the 30% low-season discount, booking steps and rescheduling rules.
excerpt: What a Rwanda gorilla permit costs, who qualifies for the cheaper rates and the 30% low-season discount, and how to book, reschedule or transfer it.
content:
A Rwanda gorilla permit costs US$1,500 per person for foreign visitors (checked October 2026) and buys one guided trek in Volcanoes National Park with a single hour beside a habituated mountain gorilla family. You book it through the Rwanda Development Board, either directly online or through a licensed tour operator, and pay in full.

The price is the easy part. The hard part is everything around it: which discounts are real, who qualifies for the cheaper resident rates, how far ahead the popular months sell out, and what happens to your money if your flight is cancelled. This guide answers each of those questions with figures checked on official Rwanda Development Board (RDB) pages, so you can book with confidence and avoid paying more than you need to.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Quick Facts

  • Foreign visitor price: US$1,500 per person per trek (checked October 2026)
  • Low-season discount: 30% off from November to May when you also stay two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe
  • Citizen and resident rates: US$200 for Rwandans and East African citizens, US$500 for other Africans and African residents (promotional, to 31 December 2026, not valid June to October)
  • Where you trek: Volcanoes National Park, north-west Rwanda, about two to three hours by road from Kigali
  • Who issues it: Rwanda Development Board (RDB), online booking portal or licensed operators
  • Minimum age: 15 years; a maximum of eight trekkers visit each gorilla family
  • Changes: Non-refundable; rescheduling costs 20% of the permit fee

How Much Is a Rwanda Gorilla Permit?

A Rwanda gorilla permit costs US$1,500 per person per trek for foreign non-resident visitors, the standard rate RDB confirmed when it announced its 2026 rates in January 2026 (checked October 2026). Rwandans and East African Community citizens pay US$200, and other African citizens and African residents pay US$500, on promotional rates.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Those promotional rates were first introduced in 2020 and have been extended year by year. The current extension runs until 31 December 2026 and excludes the peak months of June to October, so a resident trekking in August should expect to pay more than the promotional figure. Rates for 2027 had not been published when we checked, so anyone planning next year should confirm the price before paying.

Rwanda gorilla permit prices by visitor category

The table below sets out who pays what. Proof of status is checked, so carry the same document you booked with.

Visitor categoryPrice per trekProof needed
Foreign non-residentUS$1,500Passport
Foreign non-resident, November to May with the low-season discountUS$1,050 (30% off)Passport plus hotel receipt for two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe and one paid activity
Rwandan and East African Community citizens (promotional)US$200National ID, valid passport or birth certificate
Other African citizens and African residents (promotional)US$500Valid passport plus resident ID, diplomatic card or a visa showing at least four consecutive months of residence

Prices checked October 2026 from RDB's portal and its January 2026 notice as reported by KT Press and AllAfrica. Promotional rates do not apply from June to October.

What does the Rwanda gorilla permit include?

The Rwanda gorilla permit covers your place in one trekking group of up to eight people, the morning briefing at the Kinigi park headquarters, the ranger guide and trackers who locate the family, and one hour with the gorillas once you reach them. It does not cover transport from Kigali, accommodation, porters or tips, so budget for those separately.

Porters are local community members who carry your daypack and offer a steadying hand on steep ground. Hiring one is optional but sensible, and it puts money directly into villages around the park. For a fuller picture of the trek day itself, read our complete guide to gorilla trekking in Rwanda.

Is There a Discount on the Rwanda Gorilla Permit?

Yes. Foreign visitors can get 30% off a Rwanda gorilla permit from November to May by combining the trek with a stay in Akagera or Nyungwe National Park, which brings the price to US$1,050. Citizens and residents have separate promotional rates, and RDB also lists a conference discount for delegates attending events in Rwanda.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

The low-season 30% discount: how it works

According to the low-season discount page on the Rwanda Development Board booking portal (checked October 2026), the 30% discount applies from November to May. To qualify, you stay two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe with a hotel payment receipt and one paid activity, or one night in Akagera and one night in Nyungwe consecutively with the activity.

Each person earns one discounted permit per three-day, two-night stay in those parks. A second discounted trek needs a second qualifying stay. In practice this suits travellers who wanted to see more of Rwanda anyway: two nights in Akagera adds savannah game drives with elephants, giraffes and lions, and two nights in Nyungwe adds chimpanzee trekking and the canopy walkway.

Do the sums before you chase the discount. The saving is US$450 per person, so the extra nights only pay for themselves if you would have enjoyed them anyway. For most first-time visitors with a week or more, they do. Our 6 Days Rwanda Gorilla Trekking and Wildlife Safari trip, for example, already spends two nights in Akagera before the gorilla trek, which is the pattern the discount rewards; ask us to check the dates against RDB's conditions when you enquire.

Resident and citizen promotional rates

The US$200 and US$500 rates are for people who live in, or are citizens of, African countries, including expatriates with a resident ID or a long-stay visa of at least four months. They are not available to holidaymakers on a tourist visa, and staff at the park can check documents against your booking.

The conference discount

RDB's portal also offers a conference discount on gorilla trekking for visitors attending meetings and events in Rwanda. The portal page does not publish the percentage or the eligibility rules, so ask the event organiser or RDB directly before you count on it.

How to Book a Rwanda Gorilla Permit, Step by Step

You book a Rwanda gorilla permit on the Rwanda Development Board's online booking portal or through a licensed Rwandan tour operator. Either way the permit is issued in each trekker's name, against their passport, and must be paid for before the trek, because cash is not accepted at the park.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Booking directly on the RDB portal

Booking a Rwanda gorilla permit yourself takes five steps:

  1. Check availability for your chosen date on the RDB booking portal.
  2. Choose the visitor category that matches your passport or residence status.
  3. Enter each trekker's full name exactly as it appears in the passport, plus nationality and passport number.
  4. Accept the Volcanoes National Park indemnity agreement.
  5. Pay online and keep the confirmation, which you show at Kinigi on the morning of the trek.

Tour operators can also place an advance booking with a deposit of between 40% and 99% of the fee, then confirm the permit by paying the balance within the portal's 30-day window. This is how operators hold permits for clients during busy months while the rest of the trip is finalised.

Booking through a tour operator

Booking through an operator costs the same permit fee, but the operator handles the logistics around it. The trade-offs look like this:

Booking routeBest forWhat to watch
RDB portal, directIndependent travellers with a car and driver already arrangedYou must reach Kinigi for the early briefing and handle any rescheduling yourself
Licensed operatorFirst-time visitors and anyone combining Rwanda with Kenya, Uganda or TanzaniaCheck the quote lists the permit fee separately so you know what you are paying for
Lodge conciergeTravellers staying at one lodge near the parkLodges usually still book through RDB and add transfers on top

What details do you need to book?

Have each trekker's full passport name, passport number, nationality and date of birth ready, plus your preferred trek date and a back-up date. Residents need a copy of the resident ID or visa that proves the rate. Make sure the name on the permit matches the passport you will carry, because a mismatch can cause problems at check-in.

How Far in Advance Should You Book a Rwanda Gorilla Permit?

Book a Rwanda gorilla permit as soon as your dates are fixed. For the dry months of June to September and the December to February holidays, aim for at least four to six months ahead. For the wetter months of March to May and November, a few weeks to two months is often enough.

Photo: Divulge Adventures

Permits are limited because each habituated family receives only one group of up to eight visitors a day. That cap protects the gorillas from stress and human illness, but it also means a single large wedding party or tour group can take a whole family's allocation on a given day. If your trek date matters more than anything else in the trip, secure the permit before you book international flights.

Travellers who cannot find space on their preferred date have two choices: shift the trek by a day or two, or cross into Uganda, where Bwindi and Mgahinga have their own permits. Our Bwindi gorilla trekking guide explains how the Uganda side works.

Can You Cancel, Reschedule or Transfer a Rwanda Gorilla Permit?

A Rwanda gorilla permit cannot normally be cancelled for a refund, but it can be rescheduled for a fee. The RDB reschedule permit service charges a processing fee of 20% of the permit fee (US$300 on a US$1,500 permit), and requests made more than seven days before the trek are approved automatically (checked October 2026).

Changes requested within seven days of the trek need RDB's approval, so they are not guaranteed. If you simply do not turn up on the trek date, the permit expires and the money is lost. RDB's portal also lists a service to transfer an advance-booked permit to another person, with the fee depending on the permit type.

Two practical points follow. First, choose travel insurance that covers non-refundable activity costs, not just flights and hotels. Second, if you feel unwell on the morning of the trek, tell the rangers: gorillas can catch human respiratory infections, and rangers can stop a visibly ill visitor from trekking.

Insider Tips

  • Pick dates before flights: Secure the Rwanda gorilla permit first, then book flights around it
  • Use the low season: November and March to May bring the 30% discount and fewer people competing for permits
  • Insure the permit: Choose travel insurance that covers non-refundable activity costs
  • Trek twice: A second trek with a different family is often more relaxed and rewarding than the first
  • Carry your passport: Bring the passport used for the booking to Kinigi; residents should also carry their resident ID

Rwanda Gorilla Permit vs Uganda: Is the Extra Cost Worth It?

The Rwanda gorilla permit costs nearly twice as much as Uganda's US$800 Bwindi permit (checked October 2026), and for many travellers the extra US$700 buys time rather than a better encounter. Volcanoes National Park is about two to three hours by road from Kigali, while Bwindi usually means a long drive or an internal flight.

FactorRwanda (Volcanoes)Uganda (Bwindi)
Permit for foreign visitorsUS$1,500 (US$1,050 with the low-season discount)US$800
AccessAbout 2-3 hours by road from KigaliLong road transfer or a domestic flight
TerrainVolcano slopes, bamboo and open forestDense, steep rainforest
Good forShort trips, double treks, travellers short on timeLonger safaris and travellers watching the budget

Rwanda suits a three- or four-day add-on to a Kenya or Tanzania safari, and Kigali has direct flights from Nairobi. Frequently Asked Questions

These are the questions travellers ask us most often about Rwanda gorilla permits.

How much is a gorilla permit in Rwanda for foreign tourists?

A Rwanda gorilla permit costs US$1,500 per person for foreign non-resident visitors (checked October 2026). That buys one trek in Volcanoes National Park with ranger guides and one hour with a habituated gorilla family. From November to May a 30% low-season discount can bring it to US$1,050 if you also stay two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe. Confirm the current price with RDB before booking.

Can I book a Rwanda gorilla permit myself?

Yes. You can book a Rwanda gorilla permit yourself on the Rwanda Development Board's online booking portal by choosing a date, entering passport details for every trekker, accepting the park indemnity agreement and paying in full. Cash is not accepted at the park. Booking alone means arranging your own transport to Kinigi before dawn, so many travellers let a local operator secure the permit within a full itinerary.

Is a Rwanda gorilla permit refundable?

A Rwanda gorilla permit should be treated as non-refundable once paid, and a no-show on the trek date means the permit expires. Your safety net is rescheduling: RDB charges a processing fee of 20% of the permit fee, and changes requested more than seven days before the trek are approved automatically. Good travel insurance with cancellation cover is the best protection for the full amount.

What is the cheapest way to see gorillas in Rwanda?

The cheapest way to see gorillas in Rwanda as a foreign visitor is to trek between November and May and claim the 30% low-season discount, which lowers the Rwanda gorilla permit to US$1,050 when you stay two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe with a paid activity. Rwandans and East African citizens pay US$200 on the promotional rate, valid outside June to October until 31 December 2026.

How old do you have to be to get a Rwanda gorilla permit?

You must be at least 15 years old to hold a Rwanda gorilla permit and trek in Volcanoes National Park. The rule protects the gorillas from childhood illnesses and reflects how steep and muddy some trails are. Families with younger children often visit Akagera for a classic game drive instead, while teenagers of 15 and over join the gorilla trek with their parents.

Final Thoughts

A Rwanda gorilla permit costs US$1,500 for foreign visitors, or US$1,050 from November to May if you add two nights in Akagera or Nyungwe, and it should be booked months ahead for the dry season. Treat it as non-refundable, insure it, and fix your trek date before your flights.
